rendering.$description: Widget colors under each WidgetKit rendering mode. In full color, code uses the colors these tokens point to; the accented and vibrant files show what the system draws, for design review. Each token's swift entry gives the full-color code, then the accented and vibrant code after " / " where it differs. Mode: Accented.

sky-top.$description: Widget background top. Goes in containerBackground(for: .widget) so the system can remove it. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

sky-bottom.$description: Widget background bottom. Removed in accented and vibrant rendering. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

primary.$description: Primary widget content (default group). Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

secondary.$description: Secondary widget content. Full color: SalahColor.labelSecondary, which keeps 4.5:1 on every sky; the system .secondary doesn’t. Accented and vibrant: .secondary, whose hierarchy survives through opacity. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

tertiary.$description: Passed or quiet widget content (large text and marks only). Full color: SalahColor.labelTertiary, which keeps 3:1 on every sky. Accented and vibrant: .tertiary. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

accent.$description: The one accent element (next prayer name, countdown or gauge). Full color: SalahColor.accentText; accented and vibrant: .primary. Mark it .widgetAccentable(); iOS and macOS tint it white, watch faces use the face color. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

mark.$description: Time-of-day marks: timeline segments, glyphs, gauge progress. Full color: SalahColor.phase.tint. Accented and vibrant: .secondary. On watch faces, keep the full-color tint and mark it .widgetAccentable(), so marks take the face color. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

track.$description: Gauge and timeline tracks: .fill.secondary in every mode. Accessory widgets also put AccessoryWidgetBackground() behind their content. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

separator.$description: Hairlines inside widgets. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

badge.$description: Now and Stop badges. Full color: SalahColor.accentFill. Accented and vibrant: .fill.tertiary, a quiet capsule. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.

on-badge.$description: Text on a widget badge. Full color: SalahColor.labelOnAccent, which keeps 4.5:1 on the gold badge in light and dark. Accented and vibrant: .primary. Modes simulate WidgetKit rendering (full color, accented, accented on a watch face, vibrant); code never sets these colors for accented or vibrant.
